title: How to Set Financial Goals You Can Track
excerpt: Turn a money priority into a target, timeline and contribution you can review as circumstances change.
introduction: A clear goal links something you value to a practical amount and a review routine. The example is fictional and in PKR.
author: Hisab Ki Kitab Editorial Team

blocks.text: A vague goal such as ?save more? is difficult to measure. A timeline that ignores rent or required bills may also be hard to maintain.
Name the goal, estimate its cost, identify money already set aside, then divide the remaining amount by a timeline that fits your cash flow. Keep emergency reserves distinct from planned purchases.

A student wants to save PKR 36,000 for a laptop and already has PKR 12,000. With eight months available, the remaining contribution is PKR 3,000 each month, assuming no fees, price changes or withdrawals.
(36,000 - 12,000) ? 8 = PKR 3,000 per month in this example. If that amount does not fit the budget, extend the timeline or revisit the target.

items: Write down what the goal is and why it matters.
Check the current cost and money already reserved.
Choose a date that leaves room for essential bills.
Review monthly and adjust the contribution or date when needed.
Choosing a date only to motivate yourself, without checking cash flow.
Counting the same savings toward more than one goal.
Using emergency money for a planned purchase.

blocks.text: Give each priority its own label so progress is visible and one goal does not quietly consume another.
A useful financial goal is specific enough to review and flexible enough to change as your life changes.

sources.title: CFPB: Your Money, Your Goals toolkit

faqs.question: How many financial goals should I set at once?
faqs.answer: Start with the priorities you can track and fund alongside essential costs. There is no required number.

faqs.question: What if I cannot make the planned contribution?
faqs.answer: Review the budget and adjust the amount, target or timeline. Avoid borrowing just to maintain a savings target.
